title: No way to tell lore which quest binary to use, and nothing names the tracker binary it talked to
description:
MISSING CAPABILITY (not a defect), reported by opum-cli-e2e 2026-09-17 after it cost a cross-repo round trip on LCLI-529. Their acceptance example is reproduced below as they gave it.

THE GAP. There is no way to tell lore WHICH quest binary to use, and nothing in lore's output names the tracker binary it actually talked to. They checked the shipped platform binary's strings: LORE_QUEST_ACTOR, LORE_QUEST_ACTOR_KIND, LORE_QUEST_ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN, LORE_QUEST_TIMEOUT_MS -- and no binary/path variable. .lore/config.toml's [tracker] carries backend = "quest" and no command or path. So the tracker binary is ambient-PATH-only. Confirmed here: src/adapters/quest.ts resolves `options.binary ?? "quest"` and the CLI never sets it.

WHY IT MATTERS, with the real incident rather than a hypothetical. opum-cli-e2e qualifies specific candidate pairs. They invoke their harness with an explicit --lore <path> AND an explicit --quest <path>, and lore silently used a THIRD quest -- the ambient 0.7.1 installed for their own tracker. Reconcile then read pausedStatus from a quest that had not written the records, saw a status that quest did not declare, and refused. From the outside this was indistinguishable from a lore bug, and was reported as one; it took a PATH-swap experiment to find. Nothing in lore's exit code, message or envelope named the quest it consulted.

For ordinary users ambient resolution is fine and probably correct. For anyone qualifying a pair it is not.

THEIR ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLE, as written:
  LORE_QUEST_BIN=/path/to/quest lore sync --json     # or [tracker.quest] command = "..."
  -> reconcile reads pausedStatus from THAT quest, not from PATH

TWO HALVES, AND THE SECOND MATTERS MORE -- their words, and I agree. The knob is the smaller half. The larger half is SURFACING THE RESOLVED TRACKER PATH somewhere readable (lore doctor, or a field on the sync envelope) so a consumer can ASSERT which binary answered rather than assume it. Without that, this whole class of mismatch stays undetectable from the outside, knob or no knob. A knob that can be set wrong and not reported is a smaller version of the same problem.

DESIGN NOTES, to decide rather than assume:
 - There is precedent for the env-var shape: the four LORE_QUEST_* variables already exist, and src/adapters/quest.ts already accepts an injectable `binary` option -- so the seam exists and only the wiring is missing.
 - Decide precedence deliberately and document it: explicit config vs env var vs PATH. The publish-release.sh auth precedence (keychain, then NPM_TOKEN, then .npmrc) is this repository's existing model for "strict, documented, and printed".
 - Whatever resolution is chosen, print it. LCLI-488 added an auth: line to publish-release.sh for exactly this reason, and LCLI-500's notes record the sequel: a printed diagnostic that is never RETAINED answers the question only while someone is watching. Prefer a field on the --json envelope over a stderr line, since a consumer can assert on the former.
 - The same question exists for the backlog and jira adapters; check whether they are ambient-only too rather than solving quest alone.

NOT URGENT for this repository's own use: lore-cli runs one ambient quest matching its own tracker. This is for consumers who qualify pairs, which is opum-cli-e2e's entire purpose.
implementationNotes: DEDUPE PASS 2026-09-17 (OPAG-176), context for a reader arriving without LCLI-529's history: that task investigated a pausedStatus-refusal report from opum-cli-e2e and closed 2026-09-17 as NOT a lore defect -- their harness's ambient quest 0.7.1 shadowed the intended quest binary, which is exactly the missing capability this task tracks. One durable item from that investigation has not been captured anywhere else: lore 0.7.0 (confirmed pre-LCLI-503 by tag inspection) still emits a stale backlog-flavored hint on a quest-backed pausedStatus mismatch; LCLI-503 fixed it on dev but 0.7.0 will keep showing it until the next release ships. Worth a release-note line whenever that release goes out, so consumers qualifying the 0.7.0 pair aren't surprised by it.
